oewn-01756692-v.learner: to make something happen, take place, or exist.
examples: They have not the same force or rapidity, and do not produce the same expression.
The happiness which this reply produced was such as he had probably never felt before.

oewn-02145619-v.learner: to bring something out so that it can be seen.
examples: Mr. Collins readily assented, and a book was produced.
Other books were produced, and after some deliberation he chose "Fordyce's Sermons."

oewn-01624592-v.learner: to make or manufacture a product that people build.
examples: The factory produces bicycles and sends them all over the world.

oewn-02029396-v.learner: to go or travel along with someone.
examples: She was to accompany Sir William and his second daughter.
She received an invitation from Mrs. Forster to accompany her to Brighton.

oewn-02722040-v.learner: to be there along with something that happens or exists, or to be connected with it.
examples: Heavy rain accompanied the storm.
A high fever often accompanies the illness.
He accompanied his grandmother at home so that she would not be alone.

oewn-00430033-n.learner: an activity that entertains you and keeps your attention on it.
examples: He acted very wisely in leaving the girls to their own trifling amusements.
Though this gentleman dislikes the amusement in general, he can have no objection to oblige us for one half hour.

oewn-07506616-n.learner: the happy feeling you get when something entertains you.
examples: To his wife he was very little otherwise indebted than as her ignorance and folly had contributed to his amusement.
"I do not cough for my own amusement," replied Kitty, fretfully.
Dining together every evening was their habit.
Late dining left them little of the evening.

oewn-05950141-n.learner: anything you hold in your mind as being true.
examples: Every day confirms my belief of the inconsistency of all human characters.
But do not deceive yourself into a belief that I will ever recede.

oewn-05925333-n.learner: an idea that is not clear or certain, but that you put some trust in.
examples: She had a belief that the weather would turn, though she could not have said why.

oewn-01496967-v.learner: to put something in a certain place, either a real place or one you only think of.
examples: Do you consider the forms of introduction, and the stress that is laid on them, as nonsense?
Mr. Collins, much offended, laid aside his book.

oewn-02312241-v.learner: to place a duty, a burden, or a punishment on someone.
examples: The court laid a heavy fine on the company.
The new rules lay extra work on every teacher.

oewn-01547474-v.learner: to set something down so that it lies flat.
examples: He laid the newspaper flat on the floor.

oewn-07569189-n.learner: a deep sense of what another person is suffering, and sorrow felt for them because of it.
examples: I cannot consider your situation with much compassion.
Though evidently regretting that her visitors were to go, she did not seem to ask for compassion.

oewn-04836781-n.learner: the kind quality of understanding how others suffer and wanting to do something about it.
examples: She was proud that in a cause of compassion and honour he had been able to get the better of himself.

connotation.why: set against its plainer neighbour pity

oewn-07304311-n.learner: a thing that makes people feel amazed.
examples: Down they ran into the dining-room which fronted the lane, in quest of this wonder.

oewn-07525235-n.learner: the feeling that something strange and surprising stirs up in you.
examples: She stood in the great hall and stared about her in wonder.

oewn-05690411-n.learner: a state of wanting to find out more about something.
examples: The child's wonder about the stars kept her asking questions all evening.

oewn-01793089-v.learner: to make someone feel bitter or angry at being wronged.
examples: His pride does not offend me so much as pride often does, because there is an excuse for it.
You had better neglect your relations than run the risk of offending your patroness.
Why, with so evident a design of offending and insulting me, you chose to tell me that you liked me against your will?
The smell from the drain offended everyone in the room.

oewn-05660438-n.learner: the power to choose, decide, and mean to do things on purpose.
examples: She married him of her own free will.

oewn-06556133-n.learner: a legal paper in which a person says who should get their property after they die.
examples: He left the house to his niece in his will.

oewn-05992539-n.learner: a firm intention or purpose that a person holds to.
examples: She had the will to keep walking even when her feet hurt.
